title: Lovettsville air disaster
summary: Pennsylvania Central Airlines Flight 19, a new Douglas DC-3, crashed near Lovettsville, Virginia on August 31, 1940, killing all 25 aboard including U.S. Senator Ernest Lundeen. While flying at 6,000 feet on approach to Pittsburgh, the aircraft encountered an intense thunderstorm near the West Virginia border. Witnesses reported seeing a large flash of lightning shortly before the aircraft nosed over and plunged to earth in an alfalfa field with wreckage scattered over a broad area.
probable_cause: Lightning strike encountered during flight through intense thunderstorm near Lovettsville, Virginia caused loss of control and structural failure.

factors.evidence: Flight 19 encountered an intense thunderstorm near Lovettsville, Virginia at 6000 feet while flying near the West Virginia border
witnesses reported seeing a large flash of lightning shortly before it nosed over and plunged to earth
wreckage was scattered over a broad area indicating structural failure during the crash

events.text: Flight 19 was flying from Washington D.C. to Detroit with stopover in Pittsburgh at 6000 feet
Aircraft encountered an intense thunderstorm near Lovettsville, Virginia approaching the West Virginia border
Witnesses reported seeing a large flash of lightning shortly before it nosed over and plunged to earth in an alfalfa field with wreckage scattered over broad area

title: 1940 Deutsche Lufthansa Ju 90 crash
summary: The Junkers Ju 90 Brandenburg took off from Berlin Tempelhof Airport at 14:24 on 8 November 1940 with 29 people on board. Radio contact at 14:48 reported flying at 2,200 metres in clouds with icing conditions. Two minutes later the final call was made and the aircraft descended uncontrollably. Investigation found ice accumulation exceeding 1.5 inches thick had jammed the elevator controls, causing loss of altitude from 2,200 metres to ground level in three to five minutes.
probable_cause: ice accumulation on flight surfaces exceeding 1.5 inches thickness jammed elevator controls leading to uncontrolled loss of altitude

factors.evidence: ice was found on the aircraft that was more than 1.5 inches thick
in instances of this type of aircraft, severe ice accumulation had been found to jam the elevators between the tail fin end cap and the outer balancer
the radio operator reported flying in clouds
the aircraft started descending and crashed into a field after rapid descent from 2,200 metres

events.text: The aircraft took off from Berlin Tempelhof Airport at 14:24
The radio operator contacted ground at 14:48, indicating they were flying at 2,200 metres in clouds
Two minutes later, the radio operator reported icing conditions
After a final call from the aircraft at 14:58 there was no further communication from the aircraft
The Ju 90 started descending and crashed into a field with descent from 2,200 m occurring very rapidly

notes: elevator jamming confirmed by physical evidence
